svg.title: Node.js Globals (REPL list)
svg.desc: Auto-playing 56s step-by-step explainer of "Node.js Globals (REPL list)" (from img_3.png). Each step is highlighted in turn with what happens, why it matters, missing concepts added in lime, and a Node.js code example. Hover to pause.
svg.text: The list you get by typing node then pressing Tab twice: four different kinds of name, mixed together

g.text: What: The slide is the REPL's list of everything you can use without importing anything. It
mixes JS built-ins, web APIs, Node globals and core modules.
Why: Knowing which group a name belongs to tells you if it also works in the browser, and
whether you must require() it in a file.
Added: Module-scope variables like require and __dirname are not real globals at all; a new
> <Tab><Tab> // prints the list on the slide
What: Everything defined by the JavaScript language itself (the capitalised names). They
exist in every JS engine: Chrome, Firefox, Node, Deno.
Why: Code that only uses these runs anywhere JavaScript runs.
What: Node added many browser APIs (fetch, URL, AbortController, TextEncoder...) so the same
Added: fetch is global since Node 18, so simple HTTP calls need no axios / node-fetch.
What: Globals that only Node has: process (info about the running program), Buffer (raw
Why: process.env is how config and secrets reach your app; Buffer is what files and sockets
What: The lowercase names (fs, http, os, crypto...) are core modules. The REPL pre-loads
them for convenience; in a real .js file you must require/import them.
Added: Use the node: prefix, e.g. require('node:fs'), so it is obviously built-in and can
never be confused with an npm package.
What: require, module, exports, __filename and __dirname look global but are not: Node wraps
every CommonJS file in a function and passes them in as parameters.
Why: That is why each file has its own module.exports and its own __dirname.
New concept: In ES modules (import/export) they do not exist; use import.meta.dirname /
// Node secretly wraps every CommonJS file like this:
What: Four kinds of global: JS built-ins (everywhere), web APIs (browser + Node), Node-only
globals (process, Buffer), and core modules (require them in files).
Added: The module wrapper behind require / __dirname, the node: prefix, and the ESM

svg.text: Core modules need require() outside the REPL
Q: Is require a global variable?
A: No, a parameter of the module wrapper
